text:
sophie: FYI customer in APAC hitting 403s when routing through their corporate proxy. They only allow outbound to a proxy IP and deny everything else. They asked what exact egress rules we need — IPs, hostnames, headers, ports, and any proxy quirks to call out. Any quick guidance we can hand off?

raj: Short answer: require TLS passthrough (CONNECT) or a TCP proxy that preserves SNI. If the proxy terminates TLS and reissues its own cert, routing fails unless it rewrites SNI or fronting host headers exactly match. We do accept `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Real-IP` but those are for logging, not routing.

alan: We publish regioned egress ranges at https://status.redwood.com/egress-ips.json — send that. Recommend customers allow outbound TCP 443 to our hostnames and the IP ranges in that file. Example part of the JSON we publish: `{"eu-west-1": ["18.197.34.0/24","18.197.35.0/24"], "ap-southeast-1": ["54.120.10.0/24"]}` (these are illustrative; use the live URL). Also note: if they rely on DNS caching inside the proxy, they must allow DNS resolution to work for hostnames like `api.redwood-inference.com` and region CNAMEs.

sophie: Quick checklist I can paste to the customer?

raj: Yes — paste this: 
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to: `api.redwood-inference.com`, region CNAMEs (e.g., `apac.api.redwood-inference.com`), and IP ranges from our egress JSON.
- Proxy must support `CONNECT`/TLS passthrough (no MITM TLS termination) OR must forward original SNI.
- Allow outbound DNS resolution (UDP/TCP 53) to their recursive resolver or allow DoH endpoints if they use DoH.
- Allow WebSocket upgrade/long-lived TLS sessions if they use streaming endpoints.

raj: If they must MITM for inspection: they need to either allowlist our hostnames and do TLS splice (not terminate), OR install a client cert we sign (enterprise-only, security review).

lex: Practical proxy config examples — for teams running Squid that need to allow SNI passthrough, configure `ssl_bump splice` for our domains. Minimal snippet:
```
acl redwood dstdomain .redwood-inference.com .api.redwood-inference.com
ssl_bump splice redwood
ssl_bump none all

# allow CONNECT to 443
acl SSL_ports port 443
http_access allow redwood
```
This ensures Squid doesn't terminate TLS for our endpoints.

raj: For customers using AWS load balancers, recommend NLB/TCP or ALB with TLS passthrough (TLS listener + target group in TCP mode). ALB that terminates TLS will break SNI routing unless they route by host header.

alan: Also call out DNS-over-HTTPS gotchas: some proxies replace DNS results or force all DoH to a corporate resolver, which is fine as long as the resolver returns the same A records. But if they use synthetic DNS responses (private mapping), that can break our multi-region failover. Ask them not to rewrite our hostnames to internal IPs.

securitybot: Add telemetry note — metrics & logging ingestion, webhooks, and artifact uploads also use TLS 443 endpoints under `telemetry.redwood-inference.com`. If they only allow `api` hostnames, those other hostnames must be included.

infra-bot: Internal doc: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-requirements (handy checklist + IP JSON link).

sophie: Awesome. I'll send the checklist + the egress JSON link and ask them to confirm whether their proxy terminates TLS or supports CONNECT. If they terminate, I'll ask for their inspection policy and whether they can splice for our domains. Thanks all :thumbsup:

raj: If you get stuck, ping me and I can pair with their network team to test curl through their proxy. Quick test to show SNI issue:
```
# expected to work (SNI preserved)
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/ -x http://corporate-proxy:3128 --connect-timeout 10
# if proxy terminates TLS you'll see a cert with proxy CN instead of our cert
```

sophie: Copy. Closing loop after their network reply.
